faqs.question: Is the 5 Day Marangu Route recommended?
faqs.answer: It is possible for fit travelers with limited time, but it is not our first choice for acclimatization.

faqs.question: Why choose 6 Day Marangu instead?
faqs.answer: The 6 day route adds an acclimatization day at Horombo before moving to Kibo Hut.

faqs.question: Does Marangu use tents?
faqs.answer: No. Marangu uses shared mountain huts.

faqs.question: Can I join a group?
faqs.answer: Yes. Choose one of the guaranteed joining dates published on this page.

faqs.question: Is summit night difficult?
faqs.answer: Yes. It begins around midnight and reaches high altitude before the long descent to Horombo.

faqs.question: Can I add a safari?
faqs.answer: Yes. Many travelers add a Serengeti safari or Zanzibar after this shorter climb.

faqs.question: How are your Kilimanjaro guides prepared for safety?
faqs.answer: Our climbs are led by licensed and well trained Kilimanjaro guides. They are trained to recognize altitude related warning signs, complete regular health checks, manage the walking pace and respond when a climber needs to stop or descend.

faqs.question: How do you monitor climbers on the mountain?
faqs.answer: Guides check how you feel and use a pulse oximeter to monitor pulse and blood oxygen readings. They consider the readings together with your symptoms and how your condition changes over time.

faqs.question: When is emergency oxygen used?
faqs.answer: Emergency oxygen is carried for stabilization during descent or evacuation when health checks and established safety procedures show that it is needed. It is not used to help a climber continue towards the summit.

faqs.question: What happens if health checks show that continuing could be unsafe?
faqs.answer: Your guide will explain the concern, provide support and follow established mountain safety procedures. When required, the team coordinates with the national park rescue service.

faqs.question: What travel insurance is required?
faqs.answer: Your policy should cover trekking up to 6,000 metres, medical treatment, evacuation and repatriation. Helicopter support depends on weather, landing conditions and the terms of your insurance.

faqs.question: Is 6 Day Marangu better than 5 Day Marangu?
faqs.answer: For most travelers, yes. The extra day at Horombo gives your body more time to adjust before moving to Kibo.

faqs.question: Is Marangu the only hut route?
faqs.answer: Yes. Marangu is the main Kilimanjaro route that uses shared mountain huts rather than tents.

faqs.question: Are the huts private?
faqs.answer: No. The huts are shared and private rooms are not normally available on the mountain.

faqs.question: Can beginners choose this route?
faqs.answer: Yes, with proper training and equipment. The direct trail and summit night still require strong preparation.

faqs.question: Can I join a group?
faqs.answer: Yes. Choose one of the guaranteed joining dates published on this page.

faqs.question: What deposit is required?
faqs.answer: A 10 percent deposit secures your booking after the date and route are confirmed.

faqs.question: How are your Kilimanjaro guides prepared for safety?
faqs.answer: Our climbs are led by licensed and well trained Kilimanjaro guides. They are trained to recognize altitude related warning signs, complete regular health checks, manage the walking pace and respond when a climber needs to stop or descend.

faqs.question: How do you monitor climbers on the mountain?
faqs.answer: Guides check how you feel and use a pulse oximeter to monitor pulse and blood oxygen readings. They consider the readings together with your symptoms and how your condition changes over time.

faqs.question: When is emergency oxygen used?
faqs.answer: Emergency oxygen is carried for stabilization during descent or evacuation when health checks and established safety procedures show that it is needed. It is not used to help a climber continue towards the summit.

faqs.question: What happens if health checks show that continuing could be unsafe?
faqs.answer: Your guide will explain the concern, provide support and follow established mountain safety procedures. When required, the team coordinates with the national park rescue service.

faqs.question: What travel insurance is required?
faqs.answer: Your policy should cover trekking up to 6,000 metres, medical treatment, evacuation and repatriation. Helicopter support depends on weather, landing conditions and the terms of your insurance.

faqs.question: Why choose 7 Day Rongai instead of 6 Day Rongai?
faqs.answer: The seven day route divides the early northern stages and gives a steadier schedule before Kibo Hut.

faqs.question: Is Rongai less crowded?
faqs.answer: It generally has fewer climbers than Machame and Marangu because it begins on the northern side.

faqs.question: Does Rongai use huts or tents?
faqs.answer: Rongai uses tents until the descent, when the route reaches Horombo Hut.

faqs.question: Can I join a group?

faqs.question: Is hotel accommodation included?

faqs.question: Can private groups choose their own date?
faqs.answer: Yes. Private departures are available on your preferred date, subject to guide and park arrangements.

faqs.question: How are your Kilimanjaro guides prepared for safety?
faqs.answer: Our climbs are led by licensed and well trained Kilimanjaro guides. They are trained to recognize altitude related warning signs, complete regular health checks, manage the walking pace and respond when a climber needs to stop or descend.

faqs.question: How do you monitor climbers on the mountain?
faqs.answer: Guides check how you feel and use a pulse oximeter to monitor pulse and blood oxygen readings. They consider the readings together with your symptoms and how your condition changes over time.

faqs.question: When is emergency oxygen used?
faqs.answer: Emergency oxygen is carried for stabilization during descent or evacuation when health checks and established safety procedures show that it is needed. It is not used to help a climber continue towards the summit.

faqs.question: What happens if health checks show that continuing could be unsafe?
faqs.answer: Your guide will explain the concern, provide support and follow established mountain safety procedures. When required, the team coordinates with the national park rescue service.

faqs.question: What travel insurance is required?
faqs.answer: Your policy should cover trekking up to 6,000 metres, medical treatment, evacuation and repatriation. Helicopter support depends on weather, landing conditions and the terms of your insurance.

faqs.question: How do you monitor climbers on the mountain?

faqs.question: What happens if health checks show that continuing could be unsafe?

faqs.question: When should I book a northern Serengeti river crossing safari?
faqs.answer: July to October is the main planning window for northern Serengeti river activity. Booking early gives you a stronger choice of well located seasonal camps.

faqs.question: Will I see an actual river crossing?
faqs.answer: The route places you in northern crossing country during the main season, and the longer itineraries give you more time near the river. The herds and conditions decide the exact crossing moment, so your guide responds to what is happening during your safari.

faqs.question: Why spend more than one day in northern Serengeti?
faqs.answer: River activity can build quickly or remain quiet for hours. Extra time lets your guide read the herd direction, revisit promising areas and avoid treating the north as a rushed stop.

faqs.question: Can I book the route exactly as shown?
faqs.answer: Yes. The itinerary remains the foundation of your safari. We only suggest a camp-location or route-flow adjustment when your actual dates make it clearly more sensible, and we explain the change and the price before you confirm.

faqs.question: Where does the safari begin?
faqs.answer: The road safari begins in Arusha. If you are staying in Moshi, we can arrange transport to the agreed departure point.

faqs.question: Is travel insurance included?
faqs.answer: Travel insurance is not included. We recommend suitable travel and medical cover before arriving in Tanzania.

faqs.question: Who should choose the 3 Day Mount Meru Climb?
faqs.answer: It is best for strong and prepared hikers who can manage a long final day from Saddle Hut to the summit and down to Momella Gate.

faqs.question: How is the 3 Day climb different from the 4 Day climb?
faqs.answer: Both follow the same route. The 3 Day option completes the summit and full descent on Day 3, while the 4 Day option sleeps again at Miriakamba before descending on Day 4.

faqs.question: Is Mount Meru useful before Kilimanjaro?
faqs.answer: Yes. It can provide valuable trekking and altitude experience before Kilimanjaro, although every high altitude climb still requires careful preparation.

faqs.question: Where do we sleep on Mount Meru?
faqs.answer: You sleep in shared mountain huts at Miriakamba and Saddle. Your hotel in Arusha or Moshi before and after the climb is included.

faqs.question: Can I choose my own start date?
faqs.answer: Yes. This is a private climb and can start on your preferred date after park, ranger, guide and hut arrangements are confirmed.

faqs.question: Can I add a safari after Mount Meru?
faqs.answer: Yes. We can arrange Kilimanjaro, a private safari or Zanzibar after you return to Arusha or Moshi.

faqs.question: What is included in the price?
faqs.answer: The package includes private airport transfers, two hotel nights in Arusha or Moshi, gate transfers, park and hut fees, ranger arrangements, mountain crew, meals, health checks and emergency support.

faqs.question: Why does a park ranger accompany the climb?
faqs.answer: Mount Meru is inside Arusha National Park and the lower trail passes through wildlife habitat. The park assigns a ranger to accompany climbers as part of its safety arrangements.

faqs.question: How are health checks completed?
faqs.answer: Your guide asks how you feel and checks pulse and blood oxygen with a pulse oximeter. Readings are considered together with symptoms and changes over time.

faqs.question: Is emergency oxygen carried?
faqs.answer: Yes. Emergency oxygen and a first aid kit are carried for mountain emergencies. Oxygen is not used as a routine aid for continuing towards the summit.

faqs.question: Do I need travel insurance?
faqs.answer: Yes. Your policy should cover trekking up to at least 5,000 metres, medical treatment, evacuation and repatriation.

faqs.question: How do I reserve the climb?
faqs.answer: Choose your preferred private start date and send the enquiry form. We will confirm the arrangements, final price and the steps needed to complete your booking.

faqs.question: Can this Zanzibar itinerary be customised?
faqs.answer: Yes. We can add beach time, swap activities, change hotels, upgrade rooms or combine the island stay with a safari or Kilimanjaro climb.

faqs.question: What does the From price mean?
faqs.answer: It is the starting price per person for two guests sharing. Your final quotation depends on travel dates, room choice and availability.

faqs.question: Are airport transfers included?
faqs.answer: Yes. Zanzibar Airport transfers and the route transfers listed in the itinerary are included.
